description: Key chain connector - carrier and cluster boards
notes: Pinout GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare - a ground between every signal (ADR 0001 item 1). Quantity is the tracked figure chain-connectors; do not restate it. They sit carrier 1, right_thumb 2, right_hand 2, left_thumb 2, left_hand 1, with four ribbon assemblies between, and the same pinout at every one. BOXED AND KEYED, because a reversed chain connector puts 3V3 into QH. SHROUD 9.10 +/-0.15mm above the board (Wurth WR-BHD) or 9.3 +/-0.25mm (3M 303), into a 20mm cavity. SOURCE THE 2x6 FROM WURTH OR EQUIVALENT: 3M's 303 length table has no 12-pin entry at all (06/08/10/14/16/20/26/34/36/40/50). Wurth's 2x6 is 22.90mm long. MATED STACK 13.1 - 14.9mm into the 20mm cavity [TE catalog 82012 p.52, 622/636 socket: 10.5 after crimping, 12.10 MAX], so 5.1mm of spare in the worst case and 13.10mm is a hard lower bound. *** DO NOT FIT A STRAIN-RELIEF CLIP *** - it takes the stack to 16.95mm nominal and 19.60mm worst case, 0.4mm of clearance, and TE does not offer one at 12 positions anyway. STILL NOT-IN-DOCUMENT: the cable exit and ribbon bend height, so the ribbon's own turn radius is uncounted

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and SER
notes: PROPOSED by cluster-boards.md and carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. Edge-rate damping at the source, which is a DIFFERENT job from the R-TERM-CHAIN that ADR 0001 deleted - that was series TERMINATION, wrong for a line dropping on four boards. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER

description: ESD protection on the key chain signals leaving the carrier
notes: PROPOSED by carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. The chain's four signals leave the board and run the length of the body. U-TVS-SPI does exactly this job for the umbilical's three

description: Fuse on the 3V3 conductor feeding the cluster boards
notes: The 3V3 conductor runs 265mm through the body beside 12V LED power; a short on it browns out the dev-board LDO and takes the instrument down with no diagnosis. Two millimetres of board, and unretrofittable - which is why a fuse was proposed at all. Bourns MF-PSMF010X is the nearest banked part: Ihold 0.10A, Itrip 0.30A, Vmax 15V, max time-to-trip 0.5s at 1.5A, all fine. *** THE DECIDING PARAMETER IS SERIES RESISTANCE, NOT THE TRIP POINT: 1.0 TO 7.5 OHMS AT 23C. *** At the circuit's real draw of 25.8mA (18 closed keys at 1.43mA) that is 26 to 194 mV, and it is harmless for a reason worth keeping: the 74HC165's thresholds and the key pull-ups sit on the SAME rail, so the RC crossing time is independent of VCC and key-release-time does not move. THE VOLTAGE-DROP OBJECTION THEREFORE DOES NOT HOLD - it was raised against the fuse's 100mA hold current rather than the 25.8mA actually drawn, a 3.9x overstatement. STILL OPEN, AND THIS IS WHAT DECIDES IT: whether to fit the part at all, or move the protection to the source end where the drop lands on nothing. Both are live; the drop is no longer the reason to refuse

description: Selects the 74HC165 serial-input source on each cluster board
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/cluster/cluster-boards.md. Position A on the three boards that have an OUT connector: SER comes from the next board's QH. Position B on the chain-end board: SER comes from the IN pin 6 passthrough, which reaches the carrier. One link is what lets all four boards be ONE schematic instead of a special last variant

description: Pull-up on the chain-end board serial input
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/cluster/cluster-boards.md. Chain-end board only. Holds the far serial input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware instead DRIVES it from the carrier's IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail - so an end-to-end chain self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, distinguishing a broken loom from a stuck bit) becomes a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice, for one resistor
